idiom_name: Jest/Vitest typed mocks (vi.mocked / jest.mocked) with module mocking
implementation_notes: TypeScript realizations wrap the runtime mock functions of the test runner: vi.fn()/jest.fn() produce the recording double, vi.mocked(module.fn) re-types a mocked export so expectations and mockReturnValue stay type-checked, and vi.mock('...', importOriginal) replaces a module while keeping inference available through the typed import() form. The compiler acts as the contract checker - a hand-written class implementing the interface is type-safe by construction and remains the fallback for paths module mocking cannot reach - while the type helper is only a cast over the runtime mock and must be backed by an actual vi.mock/jest.mock call.
pitfalls: vi.mocked/jest.mocked only re-types an already-mocked function: forget the vi.mock/jest.mock call and the types claim a double while the real implementation still runs.
Module mocks are hoisted and cached per test file, so calls and implementations leak between tests unless mocks/modules are reset; mocking modules loaded through require() is not supported.
Casting around mocks (as unknown as T) erases exactly the checking that makes the typed double useful; prefer the runner's typed helpers and keep the collaborator interface explicit.
